doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Start date and Hey Ba-Ba-Re-Bop
summary: He joined around 1946-47; the band played Hampton's hit, which Mullins disliked but which made Hampton a fortune.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So what year did you start with him?
’45. I think it was the 1940s. 1946 or ‘47.
Because in the history of jazz books they often mention that he helped get the rhythm & blues thing going, popular. That song he did, “Hey Bop-A-Roo.”
Yeah. He made a fortune off that. I hated that. But he made a fortune. We used to play it every place we played, the band played, that was one of the numbers we played.
And you guys in the band were expected to sing back the thing, right?
